atomic_theory.definition: An atom is the smallest indivisible particle of matter. All electricity begins at this microscopic level.

parts_of_an_atom.Nucleus: The central core of the atom. It is very heavy and contains Protons and Neutrons.
parts_of_an_atom.Protons: Tiny particles with a Positive (+) charge. (Think: P for Positive).
parts_of_an_atom.Electrons: Negative (-) particles that spin in paths called orbits or shells around the nucleus. Electricity is caused when these electrons move from one atom to another.

static_electricity_details.definition: Static electricity is a type of electricity where charges gather on the surface of an insulator and remain stationary (do not flow).
static_electricity_details.production_by_friction: When you rub two insulators together, friction causes electrons to be 'ripped' from one surface and transferred to another.

the_law_of_electrostatics.rule: Unlike charges attract each other; Like charges repel each other.
the_law_of_electrostatics.visual_reference: [IMAGE_003: Attraction and Repulsion of Charges Diagram]

daily_life_examples: A plastic comb becoming charged after rubbing through hair and picking up paper.
Feeling a tiny 'zap' after walking on a nylon carpet and touching a metal door handle.
The friction of fuel flowing through pipes in aircrafts (this is why planes must be 'earthed' during refueling to prevent sparks).

lightning_and_thunder.how_lightning_forms: In storm clouds, ice and water droplets rub together, creating massive static charges. When the charge is big enough, it leaps as a giant spark (Lightning) to another cloud or the ground.
lightning_and_thunder.visual_reference: [IMAGE_004: Lightning Discharge between Clouds and Earth]
lightning_and_thunder.speed_of_light_vs_sound: We see lightning before hearing thunder because Light travels much faster (300,000 km/s) than Sound (0.33 km/s).
lightning_and_thunder.environmental_benefits: Lightning helps in 'Nitrogen Fixation'—it converts atmospheric nitrogen into nitrates in the soil, which helps plants grow as natural fertilizer.
lightning_and_thunder.dangers: Lightning can destroy tall buildings, set forests on fire, and cause instant death to humans and animals by electrocution.

lightning_protection.the_lightning_conductor: A safety device made of a thick copper or aluminum rod with pointed spikes at the top of a building.
lightning_protection.visual_reference: [IMAGE_005: Diagram of a Lightning Conductor on a House]
lightning_protection.why_pointed_spikes: Spikes leak and attract charges from the air more effectively than flat surfaces.
lightning_protection.the_grounding_system: The rod is connected to a wire that leads to a metal plate buried deep underground to neutralize the electricity safely.

essential_safety_rules.visual_reference: [IMAGE_006: Safety Poster - Do's and Don'ts of Storms]
outdoor_rules: DO: Wear rubber-soled shoes; rubber is an insulator that prevents current from entering the body.
DON'T: Seek shelter under tall trees or stand in open fields (you become the highest point).
DON'T: Swim in open water during a storm as water is a conductor.
indoor_rules: Avoid using corded telephones (lightning travels through wires).
Stay away from windows and do not touch metal water taps.
